definitions.explanation: A large, rigid suitcase or travel case. Evokes the classic rectangular hard-sided luggage, though the word is sometimes used loosely for large bags in general.
The luggage compartment at the rear of a car. This is the standard everyday word for this part of the car in Japanese.

examples.english: This car has a spacious trunk, so a golf bag fits in easily.

notes:
A loanword from English "trunk." Both senses are common in everyday Japanese.

USAGE:
For luggage, トランク evokes a traditional hard-sided rectangular case. Modern wheeled suitcases are more often called ⟦スーツケース→スーツケース：01781_suutsukeesu⟧ or キャリー⟦ケース→ケース：03841_keesu⟧, while トランク has a somewhat classic or vintage feel in this sense. For cars, トランク is the everyday word — it works for sedans and is sometimes extended to SUVs and hatchbacks, though {荷室|にしつ} (cargo area) is also used for those.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- トランク⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to open the trunk
- トランク⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{積|つ}む→積む：02294_tsumu⟧: to load into the trunk
- トランクルーム: storage room, trunk room (a rental storage unit)
- トランクス: boxer shorts (trunks — note the different word)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦スーツケース→スーツケース：01781_suutsukeesu⟧: suitcase — the standard modern word for wheeled luggage
- キャリー⟦ケース→ケース：03841_keesu⟧: carry-on case — wheeled luggage, especially cabin-size
- {荷室|にしつ}: cargo area — a more generic term for a vehicle's luggage space
